decision: Use deterministic offline Qubes readiness/qualification gates that require explicit deployment binding (expected git SHA, source Qube, target Qube, qrexec service), strict campaign framing, bounded future clock skew, and multi-run provenance consistency before REAL-WORKER READY can be emitted.
problem: Numerically clean qrexec evidence is insufficient if the gate is not explicitly bound to the exact deployment being qualified. A self-consistent report from another commit/topology, or a future-dated report accepted as age zero, could otherwise satisfy readiness checks without proving the intended environment.

reviewers.preferred: require explicit expected SHA/topology/service binding in addition to correctness counters and scenario coverage
reviewers.reason: prevents a valid-looking but unrelated campaign from qualifying the intended worker deployment

reviewers.preferred: fail closed when expected deployment binding is absent and reject provenance beyond a bounded future clock skew
reviewers.reason: removes two trust ambiguities: unbound provenance and clock-manipulated freshness

reviewers.preferred: keep validation offline inside the existing readiness gate
reviewers.reason: adds no qrexec round trips, daemon, database, or worker-side state and has negligible CPU/memory cost

alternatives.name: optional expected binding
alternatives.correctness: weaker because provenance can self-assert its own SHA/topology
alternatives.robustness: poor against accidental invocation with missing environment variables

alternatives.name: external attestation/telemetry service
alternatives.correctness: potentially stronger with trusted signing and independent clocks
alternatives.regressionRisk: higher operational and key-lifecycle surface before real Qubes evidence exists

alternatives.name: explicit offline deployment binding plus bounded clock-skew validation
alternatives.correctness: strong for the current lab-to-Qubes qualification boundary
alternatives.robustness: fails closed on missing expected SHA/Qubes/service, mismatches, stale reports, or future-dated reports beyond skew
alternatives.latency: no additional qrexec calls; constant-time metadata comparisons
alternatives.regressionRisk: low because production worker/coordinator semantics are untouched

tests: a fresh matching qrexec report with complete fencing evidence can qualify
missing all expected deployment bindings remains LAB READY
omitting any one of expected SHA/source/target/service remains LAB READY
wrong SHA or topology remains blocked
future-dated provenance beyond five-minute skew fails freshness
multi-run qualification still enforces unique run IDs, same SHA/topology, freshness, scenario coverage, and latency sample minimums
GitHub Node QA and Swift QA must both be green on the exact new head
qa.ciRequirement: Do not accept Qubes qualification evidence until Node QA and Swift QA are green on the exact head containing this gate hardening.

failuresAndLessons: Zero correctness counters do not prove the intended deployment was tested.
A provenance field is not a trust anchor when the expected value is optional; REAL-WORKER readiness must be explicitly bound to deployment intent.
Clamping negative report age to zero can accept future-dated evidence; bounded future clock skew must be checked before freshness passes.
Offline validation is currently the strongest low-regression choice, but it is not cryptographic/dom0 attestation and must not be described as such.
Real Qube-to-Qube qrexec execution evidence remains mandatory; no simulator or self-declared provenance can replace it.
